guidance: Prepare an SRS informed by ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 requirements-engineering principles. User requirements are authoritative input, not verified implementation. Separate required behavior, observed implementation, proposals and assumptions. Requirements should be atomic, unambiguous and verifiable; preserve supplied requirement IDs and never invent agreed priorities, measurements or acceptance. Do not claim full standards conformity or reproduce standard text.
notice_ru: Самостоятельно разработанная структура SRS с ориентиром на ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018: https://www.iso.org/standard/72089.html. Полный текст стандарта не воспроизводится; автоматическая генерация не подтверждает соответствие всем его требованиям.
notice_en: Independently authored SRS structure informed by ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018: https://www.iso.org/standard/72089.html. The full standard is not reproduced; generated output does not establish conformity with all its requirements.

headings.guidance: State the software purpose, system boundary, intended readers and included/excluded capabilities.
Identify supplied stakeholder roles, business goals and intended benefits; unknown contacts and approvals are TODO.
Define project terms and cite only supplied sources. Do not fabricate standards clauses or document versions.
Describe how the product fits its environment and summarize capabilities without duplicating the detailed requirements.
Describe user roles, skills, access needs and accessibility considerations supported by requirements.
Distinguish declared software/platform dependencies from required deployment environment; unknown platform versions and sizing are TODO.
Separate mandated constraints, assumptions requiring confirmation and external dependencies; mark conflicting requirements and code explicitly.
Describe required user interactions, inputs, outputs, navigation and error feedback; do not infer a graphical UI from an API.
Specify supported system integrations, data contracts and hardware interfaces; mark hardware interfaces not applicable only when justified.
Describe protocols, message/API formats, authentication requirements and failure behavior from evidence.

Write atomic, verifiable requirements with distinct IDs prefixed FR-, actor, trigger, expected behavior, source and priority if supplied. Preserve existing user requirement IDs. Code-derived requirements are proposals requiring confirmation.
Describe preconditions, normal flow, alternative/error paths and postconditions. Never claim scenarios were executed.
Describe entities, constraints, validation, persistence and lifecycle requirements; retention periods and privacy rules need supplied authority or TODO.
Describe response-time, throughput, capacity and resource criteria with sources. Do not invent numerical targets or measured performance.
Describe fault tolerance, recovery, data integrity and availability criteria. Missing SLO, RTO and RPO values are TODO.
Describe authentication, authorization, data protection and auditing requirements. Distinguish implemented controls from requirements; do not assert compliance.
Describe usability and accessibility criteria for supported user roles and interfaces; unknown acceptance thresholds are TODO.
Describe supported platforms, compatibility, configuration, diagnostics, maintenance and migration requirements; do not invent support commitments.
Propose inspection, analysis, demonstration or test for requirements with measurable expected results. Missing acceptance authority and thresholds are TODO; no test results may be fabricated.

headings.guidance: Map only requirement IDs actually present in supplied evidence to source, component and proposed verification. If generated requirements from other chapters are unavailable, use their stable section IDs and mark requirement-level links TODO; never invent cross-chapter IDs.
List unresolved decisions and conflicts requiring stakeholder confirmation; owners, approval dates and signatures are TODO if not supplied.
Document supplied priorities and allocation to delivery increments, change/version information and approval process. Unspecified schedules are TODO, not inferred from code dates.
